search_row.title: Genetic hitchhiking (selective sweep)
search_row.statement: When a favourable mutation sweeps to fixation, it reduces genetic variation at closely linked neutral sites, and the reduction is larger the tighter the linkage relative to the strength of selection.
search_row.math: the relative heterozygosity H_{after}/H_{before} at a neutral site at recombination fraction c is an increasing function of c/s that tends to 0 as c/s \to 0; the affected region has a width of order s in recombination units, up to logarithmic factors in N

fields.dct:source: John Maynard Smith (1974) The hitch-hiking effect of a favourable gene
fields.delphi:proposedTest: Test for a positive correlation between neutral diversity and local recombination rate across the genome, and for diversity troughs around sites of recent adaptive substitution, while modelling background selection as the alternative.
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: a single sweep from a new mutation, deterministic allele-frequency trajectory, two loci. Formal status: proved under these approximations (later refined in coalescent treatments). Background selection produces a similar correlation between diversity and recombination.
